notes:
Overview: Helpmate is a mid-size contact-center SaaS provider powering ~200 enterprise customers (healthcare + fintech focus). They run high-volume live-chat for merchants and want to increase automated deflection to reduce human handoffs. Very cost-sensitive; currently evaluating unit economics for 1M+ conversations/month.

Recent timeline and activity (shorthand):
- 2025-10-15: initial inbound (growth) — introduced by partner IntegrateOps.
- 2025-11-02: discovery call w/ Jordan + Maya. Needs: lower AHT, better first-response accuracy, ticket summarization for handoffs.
- 2026-01-12: demo (hosted API) — ran sample flows, latency ok but cost higher than internal target.
- 2026-02-18: deep dive POC kickoff (ff_call_2026-02-18_helpmate-demo). Scope: 4-week perf run, Zendesk + home-grown DB attachments, 3M messages sample.
- 2026-03-02: QPS and spike mode review (ff_call_2026-03-02_qps-review). Observed 3x CPU/GPU load during simulated promo bursts; need autoscale and graceful degradation strategies.
- 2026-03-04: InfoSec submitted detailed questionnaire; pending answers about KMS, audit logs, retention and residency.

Use-case / requirements (quotes and paraphrase):
- "We want agent assist for 60% of tickets, and system summaries so agents can close faster" — Head of Product.
- Primary workloads: short-turn chat (avg turn length 25 tokens), ticket summarization (longer context up to 4k), tool-calling to update CRM fields and triage.
- Latency targets: <=200ms for classification/reranking path; <=800ms acceptable for generation used in agent drafts. Throughput: target sustained 2k concurrent chats, spikes to 15k concurrent for promos.
- Cost sensitivity: target unit cost <= $0.02 per conversation (all-in) at 1M conv/month. Open to quantized models and batching to meet targets.
- Model preferences: open to using quantized Llama-family variants or distilled instruction models; fallback to smaller model during spikes.

Technical notes and POC design points: (fragments)
- POC uses a prefix cache for FAQ flows — expect high repeat rate for top-50 intents (batching + cache hit rate critical).
- Must demonstrate 3x cost reduction via batching and int8/4-bit quantization while keeping F1 for intent detection within 2%.
- Routing: prefer smart routing by policy (latency SLA for VIP customers, cheaper route for others).
- Integration: Zendesk app will call Redwood API; need example telemetry and token-level cost breakdowns for billing.
- Failure modes: want clear graceful degradation: fast fallback to classification-only model when KV cache miss or GPU saturated.

Commercial / legal:
- Interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation, but may start on Hosted to shorten time-to-value. Devil's in the pricing — procurement needs clear ARR modeling.
- Legal: data residency for EU customers (contracts require EU-only storage), add-ons: SOC2 + ISO certs required.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver perf run report (Maya) with token-level cost and latency percentiles by 2026-03-10.
- Show quantization impact matrices and recommended batch sizes.
- Jordan to prep SOW draft for Dedicated 12-month commit (estimated ARR range above).
- InfoSec to get answers on KMS + audit logs; CSM Liam looping in if proof-of-concept passes.

Open questions / blockers (shorthand):
- Can Redwood guarantee throughput for 15k concurrent spikes with autoscale policy?
- Exact per-conversation pricing at 1M+ monthly convs with mixed model routing.
- How will cold-start latency behave when a new conversation hits cache?
- Legal: can user-level transcripts be restricted to EU region for certain tenants?

Linked artifacts: pricing-deck-helpmate.pdf (drive), ff_call_2026-02-18_helpmate-demo (Fireflies), Zendesk integration notes (gmail thread).

Representative CRM-style comment: "POC is promising — if perf-run shows 2.5x reduction in unit cost with acceptable QA delta, procurement moves fast. Otherwise, stalled on price."
